analysis.title: The Day Ahead - North America, Thursday, November 19, 2026
key_insights: US stocks closed mixed on Nov 18: DJIA -1.11% to 50,198.17, S&P 500 -0.23% to 7,323.63, Nasdaq Composite +0.42% to 24,429.89. The S&P reversed early gains after the Fed minutes.
Fed minutes of the October 27-28 meeting showed officials saw growing risk they would need to intensify efforts to control inflation, though rates were held steady.

Fed Governor Waller said on CNBC the Fed should approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027. Jefferies' Simons called Waller the leader of the most hawkish commentary and said the market does not price a 50bp hike as a baseline.

The dollar index rose 0.28% to 103.77, touching a 19-month high, on expectations of a rate hike next month. EUR/USD fell 0.20% to 1.0975 and GBP/USD fell 0.44% to 1.3150 after UK underlying inflation held steady in October.

Treasury yields: 10-year 5.0643%, 2-year 4.7978%, 5-year 4.8805%, 30-year 5.4067%. Longer-dated yields fell with oil, and Waller's comments limited the decline. The $16B 20-year auction priced at a 5.459% high yield with a 2.63 bid-to-cover.

Oil fell after EIA data showed US crude stocks up 3.4M barrels to 417.8M (Reuters poll expected +58,000) and gasoline stocks up 5.2M to 215.9M (poll +1.6M). WTI fell 3.63% to $82.89 and Brent fell 1.67% to $91.58.

Spot gold fell 3.23% to $3,725.30/oz on the hawkish Fed signals and a stronger dollar and yields. Analyst Tai Wong sees a probe of 3350-3450 in coming weeks barring a quick reversal. Copper fell 5.25% to $5.66/lb.

Nvidia fell 2.89% to $150.96 after its results. Its forecast eased demand concerns, but the CEO succession after Jensen Huang's exit is the central issue. HSBC said the stock may struggle until a permanent CEO is named. Interim CEO Colette Kress said it is business as usual.

Anthropic's IPO is expected to price Thursday at a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, raising up to $64.4B by selling 825M shares. At least 11 leveraged single-stock ETFs from seven issuers are being prepared, and options could start trading as soon as Monday.

Retail earnings: Target beat for a third straight quarter (comps +5.6% vs 3.5% est) and raised 2026 sales growth guidance to 6% from 5%. TJX raised its full-year outlook and rose 8.04% to $140.29. Lowe's reaffirmed adjusted EPS of about $12.25, 3 cents below estimates, with gross margin at 32.95% vs 34.19% a year earlier.
Thursday's earnings calendar: Walmart (07:00), Williams-Sonoma (BMO), and Intuit, Keysight and Ross Stores (AMC). Gap is also expected to report.

Thursday's data: initial jobless claims (poll 197,000, prior 200,000), continuing claims (poll 1.710M), Philly Fed Business Index for November (poll 20.0, prior 20.9), and Leading Index for October (poll 0.0%).
Software and cybersecurity led the S&P 500: Okta +11.72%, Palo Alto Networks +8.69%. Managed care fell: Humana -12.92%, UnitedHealth -10.30%, Elevance -7.70%.
US single-family housing starts rose 4.0% to 864,000 in October, but permits fell 8.7% to 772,000, the lowest since January 2023.
The Trump administration is weighing requiring US companies to publicly disclose their use of Chinese AI models.
TSX fell 2.09% to 34,578.05, with materials down 5.42% on the gold slide. Canadian inflation held at 3.1% in October.

earnings_insights: Walmart Q3 (reports 07:00 ET Thursday): LSEG IBES EPS estimate $0.64 vs $0.62 year ago, revenue estimate $187,271.11M.
Intuit Q1 (AMC Thursday): EPS estimate $2.70, Smart Estimate $2.84, year ago $3.34, revenue estimate $4,305.45M.
Keysight Q4 (AMC Thursday): EPS estimate $3.37 vs $1.91 year ago, revenue estimate $1,945.92M.
Ross Stores Q3 (AMC Thursday): EPS estimate $1.88, Smart Estimate $1.93, year ago $1.58, revenue estimate $6,255.39M.
Williams-Sonoma Q3 (BMO Thursday): EPS estimate $2.18, Smart Estimate $2.19, year ago $1.96, revenue estimate $1,998.30M.
Gap is expected to post a rise in Q3 revenue (estimate only, no figure given) while discretionary spending remains pressured.

Target reported Q3 comparable sales +5.6% vs LSEG estimate of 3.5%, traffic +5%, digital comps +9.8%, apparel sales -3.8%, home decor +2.5%. It raised 2026 sales growth guidance to 6% from 5% and said November sales trend above October. Capex is planned at $5B-$6B in 2027.

TJX reported Q3 revenue of $15.95B vs LSEG average estimate of $15.84B and adjusted EPS of $1.34, in line with expectations. It guided FY2027 comps +4% (prior 3%-4%) and adjusted EPS $5.17-$5.20 (prior $5.15-$5.20).

Lowe's reaffirmed FY adjusted EPS of about $12.25, 3 cents below LSEG estimates. Q3 gross margin was 32.95% vs 34.19% a year earlier. It cut its operating margin forecast to about 11.5% from 11.6% and reported a benefit of nearly $250M from tariff refunds.
Nvidia reported Q3 results on Tuesday with revenue and earnings above expectations and a forecast above Wall Street estimates.

risk_factors: A faster Fed hiking pace: Waller wants a 50bp hike in December or a faster pace of hikes in 2027, and the minutes show some officials open to a bigger move.
Nvidia CEO succession uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit, which HSBC says may cap the stock until a permanent CEO is named.
AI stock weakness: hyperscalers and AI-linked stocks have lost ground in recent weeks.
Fuel and transportation costs are squeezing retailer margins, as at Lowe's.
A stronger dollar and higher yields pressure gold. Wong sees a probe of 3350-3450.
Meta's Muse AI agent has had safety incidents, including exposure of private messages, according to internal posts.
vol_and_positioning: At least 11 leveraged single-stock ETFs from seven issuers are being prepared for Anthropic's IPO, with retail investors accounting for much of the interest.
Options on Anthropic shares could begin trading as soon as Monday, with heavy interest expected.

Jefferies' Simons said the market does not price a 50bp hike as a baseline, but the possibility of a 50bp move or two in a row adds some expectation of a higher overnight rate over the next two years.
geopolitical: Trump and Putin shook hands with Xi Jinping beside them at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18.
The Trump administration is weighing requiring US firms to disclose Chinese AI model use, an approach that avoids new restrictions that could anger industry or Beijing.
Canada is re-engaging with China step by step and widening financial-firm market access, while it negotiates trade with the US.
Canada discussed with Mexico joining the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank. The UK will not join and Germany is an observer.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia's strong forecast showed the product roadmap and demand are intact. Counterpoint says results stabilized sentiment and put a floor under the AI selloff.
tension_points.bear_case: Counterpoint says results postponed rather than cured investor anxiety. HSBC says the stock may struggle until a permanent CEO is named and new leadership delivers planned products.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Naming a permanent CEO and new leadership delivering planned products would ease the cap on the stock, per HSBC.

tension_points.bull_case: The market does not price a 50bp hike as baseline, per Jefferies' Simons, so a standard-size hike would not surprise.
tension_points.bear_case: Waller wants a half-point hike in December or a faster 2027 pace, and the minutes show a couple of officials broached 50bp if inflation disappoints.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 50bp hike in December, or two large hikes in a row, would add to expectations for a higher overnight rate over the next two years.
